title: Non-overlapping Intervals
statement:
Find the fewest intervals you have to remove from a list so that none of the intervals left overlap.

The first line is the number of intervals `n`, which can be 0. Each of the next `n` lines is one interval as `start end`, two whole numbers where `start` is less than `end`. The intervals can come in any order, and the same interval can appear more than once. Two intervals overlap when one starts before the other ends. Intervals that only touch, like `1 2` and `2 3`, don't overlap, so both of them can stay. Print the smallest number of intervals to remove.

Input:

```text
4
1 2
2 3
3 4
1 3
```

Expected output:

```text
1
```
hints: Think about which intervals to keep instead of which to remove. Keeping as many as you can means removing as few as you can.
Of all the intervals, the one that ends first leaves the most room for the others. Sort by end, not by start.
Walk the sorted list and remember where the last interval you kept ends. An interval that starts before that end has to go. Any other one is kept, and its end becomes the new one to beat.
